narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated an 86% probability that you would represent a bad credit risk. In practical terms, this is a strong indication that, based on the information available, repayment problems are more likely than for a typical approved applicant, so the bank declined the request.

Three factors drove this decision most strongly, in ranking order. The most influential was your checking-account status: an account below zero is uncommon among approved applicants and pushed the assessment toward bad credit. The second was your credit history, recorded as all credits paid at the bank; because only about 3% of approved applicants show this specific history, it added to the risk signal rather than offsetting it. The third was property status: having no known property or assets was also uncommon among approved applicants and pushed toward bad credit. Your requested duration was close to the approved average, and the amount was lower than average, but those did not outweigh these top concerns.

To improve a future application, first resolve the negative checking-account position and keep the account in good standing. Review your credit record for errors and build a longer, consistent repayment history. Provide evidence of assets, savings, or a guarantor if available, and consider reducing the amount or installment burden. Ask the bank which specific records it needs updated before reapplying.
